notes.crypto: DSS reports intact or broken over the signature value and every reference; xml-sec reports the XMLDSig status of the first signature. Both are independent of trust.
notes.structure: DSS reports its format label; xml-sec reports met or unmet for the step's level (EN 319 132-1 §6), or the outcome that stopped the level. A format label is not a conformance verdict.
notes.trust: DSS reports indication/subindication under its default policy with the run's root as the only anchor. xml-sec gives no trust verdict: statuses are the caller's reading. B-B and B-T stay INDETERMINATE/CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_GENERAL_FAILURE for DSS because no revocation data exists before B-LT.
notes.preserved: SignedInfo and SignatureValue of the B-B signature appear byte for byte in every later document.
notes.Tokens: xml-sec under TimestampTokenEncoding::Declared refuses a token DSS made: BouncyCastle writes its certificate SET OF unsorted, which is not DER, and an unmarked token is DER (EN 319 132-1 §5.1.3). Normative difference, intended.
notes.unmet: Under TimestampTokenEncoding::Ber xml-sec reads DSS's tokens and finds DSS's B-T met, but not the B-LT and B-LTA DSS makes: DSS places the CRL that covers the TSA certificate only in RevocationValues, while EN 319 132-1 §6.3(x) requires the validation data of a time-stamp in TimeStampValidationData, AnyValidationData or the token itself. Normative difference, intended. xml-sec therefore refuses to renew such an archive (§6.3(aa)).
notes.revoked: The CRL lists the signer as revoked before signing. DSS refuses to augment to B-LT or to renew; xml-sec adds the evidence, because a level states what the document carries, and DSS then reads it as INDETERMINATE/REVOKED_NO_POE.
notes.crl: Every certificate of the run carries a CRL distribution point that is never fetched: DSS looks a CRL up only through one (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.13), while the run supplies the CRLs offline.
